summary: The 13th Dalai Lama worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Agvan Dorzhiev (circa 1898–1904), Pa Ri Rabsal, Tertön Sogyal, Lobsang Lungtok Tenzin Thinley, and Gendun Tendzin Gyatso, and taught numerous prominent figures.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, the 14th Dalai Lama studied under teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1948–1983), Trijang Lobsang Yeshe Tenzin Gyatso (1951), Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded INEB (1989) and Mind and Life Institute (1990).

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje studied under Kalu Rinpoche, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He taught numerous students, including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, and Reginald A. Ray.
The 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, and Khangsar Dorje Chang.

id: P:3rd Sras Rinpoche Thubten Kalsang Bstanpai Gyaltsen
summary: A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under the 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga, at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1971), and Gyume Tantric College (1971). He held posts at Rizong Monastery, Drepung Loseling (1984), and Gyume Tantric College (1995–2008).

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Drepung Monastery (circa 1951–1959). He held teaching and leadership positions at Central School for Tibetans, Shimla (1960), Central School for Tibetans (1965–1970), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Ayu Khandro. He taught Chatral Sangye Dorje and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche.
Krishnaswami Ayyangar studied at Pachaiyappa's College (circa 1908–1911). He subsequently worked at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as Professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).
An indologist, A. B. Gajendragadkar held posts as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College.
A scholar in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, McDermott studied under W. Norman Brown and held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 1969).

Muller works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Stony Brook University under Sung-Bae Park, and held posts at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019).
Active in Indology and linguistics, A. Fürst studied at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe.
Working in Indology and religious studies, Mohan studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1971 to 1989. He founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

Armstrong was a philosophy scholar who studied at Jesus College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Swansea, University of Malta, Cardiff, and the University of Liverpool (1950–1972), with visiting positions at Manhattanville and Dalhousie, and founded Dionysius in 1977.

Working in history, archaeology, and philosophy, Sabra studied at Alexandria University, University of London, and the London School of Economics under Karl Popper (circa 1951–1955). He held posts at the Warburg Institute (1962–1972) and Harvard University (1972–1996).

An Indologist and linguist, Ramanujan studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Indiana University Bloomington. He served as a fellow at Deccan College and taught at MS University of Baroda, Harvard, and the University of Chicago (1962–1993).
A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Sastri served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (circa 1891–1916) and as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (circa 1916–1926).

An Indology scholar, Aiyangar studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar. He served as Joint Editor for Brahmavidya at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and as Librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

Narasimhia, who worked in linguistics and Indology, completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (circa 1930–1933). He held posts at Maharaja's College, Mysore (circa 1934) and the University of Mysore.
